summary: ORBIT 2.0 – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is a browser-based 3D learning experience that introduces players to lunar exploration and astronaut operations. Players take on the role of an astronaut, inspect their spacesuit, explore the lunar surface, collect three lunar samples and return to the habitat. In the second mission, players deploy an additional solar array, activate a power console and manage simulated operating hours. By combining interactive exploration with simplified resource-management tasks, ORBIT 2.0 aims to make space-mission concepts more engaging and easier to understand. The project is inspired by real lunar exploration, particularly the Apollo 17 mission at the Taurus–Littrow valley. Developed by Team ORVEXIA.
details:
ORBIT is a browser-based 3D lunar mission training experience designed to introduce players to astronaut activities and lunar outpost operations.

The project allows players to experience two missions. In Mission 01, players inspect their spacesuit, explore the lunar surface, collect three lunar samples and return to the habitat. In Mission 02, players deploy an additional solar array, activate a power console and manage simulated operating hours.

The main goal is to make lunar exploration concepts more engaging through interactive gameplay rather than relying only on theoretical explanations. Players can explore the environment, interact with objects and complete mission objectives.

The experience was developed as a web-based 3D game and can be accessed through a browser. It includes keyboard and mouse controls, along with mobile controls.

ORBIT is inspired by real lunar exploration, particularly the Apollo 17 mission at the Taurus–Littrow valley. It aims to encourage curiosity about space exploration, astronaut responsibilities and the challenges of operating a lunar habitat.

Developed by Team ORVEXIA.
